clauses.reason: The order closes the listed agencies all day on December 24, 1954 and one-half day on December 31, 1954 and excuses employees on those two days only. It ended by its own terms at the close of December 31, 1954, the second and last day; the December 24 closing was spent at the close of that day. No later order is held that revokes, extends or amends it, and Executive Order 10358, cited for the meaning of holiday, is an earlier order that does not reach it.

research_rationale:
EO 10580 (signed 1954-12-04 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-12-06, 11:32 a.m.; 19 FR 8037, Federal Register of December 7, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10580.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one operative sentence with two joined commands limited to two days. First, the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia, including the General Accounting Office, the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations, are closed all day on Friday, December 24, 1954 and one-half day on Friday, December 31, 1954. Second, federal employees in that area and in the field service, except those excluded for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law, are excused from duty on that day and that half day, each of which is a holiday within the meaning of Executive Order 10358 and of the statutes on compensation and leave. There is no recital, report deadline, extension or renewal. First end: by its own terms the order operates only on those two days, so it was fully performed at the close of December 31, 1954; the December 24 closing was spent earlier. The text has no until-wording, so the end is the last stated day. Later instruments: EO 10358 (June 9, 1952; held as actor context and read) predates this order, is cited only for its definition of holiday and supersedes only EO 9636 (its section 8); it cannot end this order, and the dossier's missing line about EO 10358 and the one OFR-catalog hit concern that citation. A scan of every held order text for the bare number 10580 found no order text that names it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

savings.reason: The order has no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. Pay and leave for the excused day and half day follow the compensation and leave statutes and Executive Order 10358, which the order invokes but does not extend, so nothing keeps the order operative after December 31, 1954.
